bull_bear.body: Capital adequacy 21%, leverage 4.9x — precisely the level at which the last capital-raise evaluation happened (the analyst pulled this from deck page 42). Management's sequence is explicit and unusually clear: **(1) dilute BHFL from 86.7% to 75% — "we have time and we are in no hurry"; (2) only then, and only if growth accelerates, consider a capital raise; and in the meantime (3) run profit growth ahead of balance-sheet growth as the primary way to build resilience.** *"We don't foresee raising capital."* Surplus earnings are being routed into the balance sheet rather than to shareholders — the INR296 cr overlay is the visible instance, justified against a INR6.3–6.5 lakh crore balance sheet. A dividend has been paid and will mechanically lift Q2 ROE. Reinvestment priorities named: AI/digital, gold-loan and MFI network, customer-centricity and design-thinking units, and two unnamed new businesses.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Geopolitics (West Asia) and monsoon / super El Nino** — the two named drivers of the INR296 cr overlay, and both flagged as *inflationary* for cost of funds. Monsoon "should be behind us in 30 days" but "we still have some distance to cover."
- **Quality of consumer growth.** Half of the ~40% consumer-finance growth is SKU price inflation, and OEMs are signalling *further* price rises — management itself called this "further risk."
- **Rising incremental cost of funds** (30–60bps in the market) against a stock CoF that has only just stabilised; guidance is range-bound "with a slight upward bias."
- **BHFL attrition under intense mortgage competition** — the one blemish on an otherwise pristine subsidiary; balance-transfer churn is structural in prime housing.
- **AI token cost as adoption scales.** Management was candid that the first two levers (use-case economics, engineering choices) are handled but the third — cost rising with firm-wide adoption — is *"a line to watch for."*
- **Overlay policy is undeclared.** Asked whether the macro overlay becomes a permanent phenomenon or releases into profit, the answer was "quarter at a time"; direction of overlay creation will only be clarified next quarter. Earnings are therefore management-smoothed by an undisclosed amount.
- **Gold-price dependency in the fastest-growing book.** Gold at $4,000–4,100 has expanded the *denominator* (a customer can now raise INR8–10 lakh against holdings that supported far less at $2,000). Management conceded: at $2,500 "the fourth point will go away" — origination sizes shrink even if the rest of the thesis holds.
- **Gold-loan competitive influx** — "every Tom, Dick and Harry wants to enter this space" (analyst framing, undisputed), against RBI's tightened comprehensive gold-loan regulations effective 1 April.
- **Succession.** The MD's term ends March 2028 with the decision deferred to December 2027 – January 2028 — an 18-month open question on the most identified-with CEO in Indian NBFC.
- **Key-person absence on the call itself:** CFO Sandeep Jain absent, and Rajeev repeatedly deferred margin/guidance specifics to him — some answers were softer than they would otherwise have been.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Unusually confident and openly so — an analyst noted he "sound[s] much more confident this quarter than at least I've heard in the last 10–15 quarters." What raises the quality read is that the confidence did **not** convert into a guidance upgrade. Asked three separate times (AUM corridor, credit cost, NIM) to raise numbers off an excellent quarter, he refused each time and pre-empted the interpretation: *"It's not lack of confidence. It's just being conscious of the fact that what we say, we stay with."* He was equally direct about what he will not opine on — *"I can't speak about the macro. I'm not a macro person. I'm a micro person"* — and reframed risk as agency rather than environment: *"risk decisions are the choices we make… Risk doesn't hold the company back. It propels the company forward."* Disclosure was granular to a fault (he volunteered that the labour code cost exactly INR60 cr / 10bps "since you count decimals"). On AI he let the COO answer the cost question in technical detail and conceded an open risk rather than claiming victory. On the "can ROE reach 24%" question he explicitly declined to maximise: *"if I was to maximize, the answer is yes. But… I'm interested in long-term sustainability."*
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The overlay is a guidance instrument, not a credit signal.** INR296 cr taken in a quarter where credit metrics improved on every cut means reported credit cost is now partly a policy variable. The tell is the framing — Rajeev answered a *numerator* question with a *denominator* answer ("you're looking at the numerator of my provisions. I'm looking at the denominator, which is that we will have INR6,30,000–6,50,000 cr of balance sheet"). Expect overlays to scale with the balance sheet, which structurally caps reported ROE upside even in good years.
- **Half of the headline consumer growth is inflation, and management said so unprompted.** A 49%/38% rural/urban print reads as a demand boom; it is roughly 20% price and 20% volume. If SKU prices flatten, reported growth halves without anything going wrong operationally — and BFL's own smartphone data (industry shipments −13–15%, BFL volumes +20–23%, ATS +30–33%) shows the *unit* market is actually contracting.
- **Gold loans are being built as a distribution business, not a lending business.** The economics are stated as branches × INR14 cr at maturity. That makes branch adds — not AUM — the leading indicator, and it means the current INR29–31k cr guidance is deliberately ~20% below the estate's own capacity. It also explains why an integrated-branch model was abandoned: only 80 of 1,700 branches are integrated, all legacy.
- **The ETB ratchet is the quiet compounding machine.** ETB moved 60% → 63%, and management put a number on the second-order effect: *"3% movement and 16 million loans will lead to lower credit cost is given."* This is the mechanism behind the three-year "lower NIM, lower opex, lower credit cost" shape — a deliberate trade of headline margin for structurally lower cost and risk, which most NIM-focused models will read as deterioration.
- **The AI disclosure is unusually falsifiable.** Rather than a transformation narrative, management gave a scoreboard with dates: 27 bots, 17 of 118 agentic apps, 71% of DIY service, INR517 cr of AI-insight-sourced disbursements, INR2,500 cr AI-bot disbursements against an INR11–12k cr full-year target, and three dated go-lives (B2B model Q2, B2C Oct–Nov, consumer AI platform May–June '27). Every one of these can be marked to market next quarter.
- **The distribution reversal is a strategic admission.** After 7–8 quarters of flat-to-declining branches on the view that "India is covered", the bottoms-up review concluded the opposite. Reopening physical expansion at 170–250 branches a year — with an explicit 2–3 year payback — is a deliberate acceptance of near-term opex drag for coverage BFL had assumed it already had.
- **Capital sequencing pre-empts an equity-raise overhang.** By stating BHFL dilution comes *first*, at 4.9x leverage and 21% CAR, management has effectively told the market it will not tap equity in FY27 — and the ROE arithmetic improves for free as the excess-capital drag reduces.
- **A rare open succession clock.** Term to March 2028, decision December 2027 – January 2028. For a franchise this identified with one executive, the 18-month build-a-resilient-business framing reads as deliberate institutionalisation ahead of that decision — which is also the most plausible reading of the "bulletproofing" language.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Long-term guidance corridors on the consolidated entity: AUM growth 23%-25%, profit growth 23%-24%, ROA 4.3%-4.7%, ROE 19%-21%, GNPA <1.4% and NNPA <0.5%.
- Conservative leverage standards: the deck shows a declining leverage threshold (7.0 stepped down to 6.0) with leverage ratio of 4.9 at Jun'26 and a footnote that "Standalone leverage is approximately 4.3X as of 30 June 2026"; capital adequacy was 20.90% with Tier-1 at 20.01% as of 30 June 2026.
- Liquidity discipline: liquidity buffer of ₹ 17,847 crore (BHFL ₹ 2,516 crore) as of 30 June 2026, and the ALM pages report daily average LCR of 231% and 158% against a regulatory requirement of 100%.
- Funding mix philosophy - "create a balanced mix of wholesale and retail borrowings with a focus on long term borrowings": consolidated borrowing mix for Money Markets : Banks : Deposits : ECB at 50% : 30% : 15% : 5%; Bajaj Finance standalone borrowings of ₹ 348,475 crore mixed 48% : 25% : 7% : 20% between money markets, banks, ECB and deposits; BHFL borrowings of ₹ 1,10,546 crore mixed Banks : Money market : NHB at 38% : 52% : 10%.
- Subsidiary capitalisation history at BHFL: capital infusion of ₹ 328 crore prior to FY18, ₹ 2,000 crore on 3 April 2024 via rights issue and ₹ 3,560 crore on 16 September 2024 through fresh issue (IPO).

bull_bear.body:
- Large, diversified customer franchise of 119.33 million with high cross-sell potential (75.51 million cross-sell franchise)
- Omnichannel distribution with 4,098 physical locations and 242,000 active distribution points plus 86.63 million app users
- Among the best-capitalised large NBFCs in India with CRAR of 21.55% and Tier-I of 20.67%

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Credit risk from unsecured lending and macroeconomic stress — Elevated leverage, higher interest rates, and asset quality concerns led to higher provisioning. The company discontinued lending to customers with multiple unsecured loans and strengthened underwriting standards to mitigate potential losses.
- Liquidity risk in tight systemic conditions — The company manages liquidity through a Board-approved ALM framework and maintains buffers (LCR at 128%, buffer of â¹15,020 crore) to meet obligations and support growth even in stressed markets.
- Operational risk from inadequate processes, systems, or fraud — Operational risk framework addresses internal process failures, human factors, and external events. Fraud control analytics are embedded in loan origination, and employees can flag suspicious activity.
- Interest rate risk on investment portfolio and NIM — Exposure arises from fixed/floating rate assets and liabilities with differing maturities. Managed via duration gap analysis, VaR, PV01, and a prudent investment policy focused on government securities and liquid funds.
- Geopolitical and macroeconomic volatility — Geopolitical developments may influence inflation, interest rates, liquidity, and capital flows, impacting growth, asset quality, and funding conditions. The company monitors these emerging risks through its governance framework.
- Foreign currency risk from ECB borrowings — Exposure to currency fluctuations on External Commercial Borrowings is fully hedged for the entire tenure as per Board-approved policy, mitigating potential mark-to-market or cash flow impacts.
- Data privacy and cybersecurity threats — Security threats endanger customer data and disrupt operations, coupled with legal liabilities, regulatory investigations, and reputational damage. The company has a structured data privacy framework and strong commitment to protecting personal data.

business.body:
- **Gold loans (+112% YoY, 4% of AUM).** Seven years in the business, "cracked it in November '23" by converting it into a *company within a company*. Model is standalone gold-loan branches, not integrated ones — only 80 of 1,700 are integrated, all legacy pre-'23. Strategy reduced to two things: network expansion and process excellence. 95% of customers are self-employed; the pitch is low friction, low entry/exit cost, small working-capital tickets and lighter credit filters (even after RBI's comprehensive gold-loan regulations came into force 1 April). **25% of gold-loan business now originates on the digital platform — management calls this "our principal moat."**
- **Consumer B2C — rural +49%, urban +38%.** Roughly half of that is SKU price inflation. Smartphones are the standout: industry shipments fell 13–15% last quarter (Counterpoint), yet BFL's smartphone volumes grew **20–23%** with average ticket size up **30–33%** — driven by a rising Apple mix and OEM-wide ATS inflation. Appliance ticket sizes are **flat** (the ~10% GST cut on air-conditioners has been fully offset by commodity-price increases). Management attributes the volume out-performance purely to affordability penetration and deeper mining of the existing franchise.
- **MSME / business & professional loans (+2%).** Under deliberate risk-led pruning since July last year; growth returns Q3. Bureau data on BL, PL and professional-loan portfolios is improving YoY across the board.
- **MFI.** Branch build-out under way — one of the two named drivers of the opex/NTI uptick alongside gold.
- **Deposits (INR68,500 cr, 15% of balance sheet).** Increasingly the structural answer to the cost-of-funds question.
- **BHFL (86.7% held).** Highest-ever quarterly AUM addition; disbursements +33%, AUM +24%, PBT/PAT +23%, ROE 12.5%, opex/NTI 19.6% (from 21%), asset quality "pristine" at 29bps GNPA / 12bps NNPA. The honest negative: **"they continue to remain under pressure on attrition, given the intense competitive activity in the business"** — mortgage balance-transfer churn is real. Stake must come down 86.7% → 75%.
- **BFSL (securities).** Strong AUM growth; PAT growth "softer" at 22% as the business matures; scale-up plans continue.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Franchise depth as the answer to competitive intensity.** Asked about PL and MSME competition (PSU banks, private banks and non-banks, "five, six competitors"), Rajeev's entire answer was the franchise: cost of originating a customer, cost of managing, cost of cross-sell and cost of credit all fall as the base is mined. Evidence given on the same call: **ETB (existing-to-bank) contribution rose to 63% from ~60%**, and he quantified the consequence — *"3% movement and 16 million loans will lead to lower credit cost is given actually."*
- **Digital origination in gold loans (25% of the book)** — named explicitly as "our principal moat", and a structural differentiator versus branch-only gold lenders.
- **Own-app scale:** 70% of app traffic is ETB, 30% NTB (payments, ASO-driven downloads) — an acquisition funnel competitors have to pay for.
- **Risk thresholds as a durable choice, not an outcome.** Bureau-tracked, line-of-business by line-of-business, BFL runs at **30–35–40% of industry 30 DPD and 60 DPD** — a self-imposed ceiling maintained since COVID. Vintage curves across 3/6/9 MOB are now **below the FY20 pre-COVID benchmark**.
- **AI cost discipline as an actual capability:** an internal token "calculator", a rule that any AI use case must cost 1/3 to 1/5 of the human alternative (voice AI runs at ~1/3), open-weight models plus an in-house RAG/context layer routing to local models, and flash/mini models instead of full-size LLMs. *"If OCR for two version documents can solve the problem why use AI."*

business.body:
- Stated identity: "A diversified non-bank with a deposit taking license", "Focused on mass and affluent segments, leveraging cross-sell to drive lifetime value", with a "business construct ... to deliver a sustainable ROA of 4.3%-4.7% and ROE of 19%-21% in the long term".
- "BFL 3.0 - A FINAI Company": ambition to "be the pre-eminent choice which meets all financial services needs of its 200 MM customers", via an "AI enabled technology architecture that integrates AI across all its processes to deliver significant operating leverage and create a virtuous growth cycle".
- Well-diversified balance sheet: consolidated lending AUM mix for Urban : Rural : MSME : Commercial : Mortgages stood at 30% : 12% : 13% : 13% : 32%; Bajaj Finance standalone AUM mix for Urban : Rural : SME : Commercial : Mortgage stood at 41% : 16% : 18% : 15% : 10% as of 30 June 2026.
- Credit standing: long-term borrowing rated AAA/Stable by CRISIL, ICRA, CARE and India Ratings, short term A1+, FD programme AAA (Stable) by CRISIL & ICRA; S&P Global issuer ratings BBB/Stable (long term) and A-2 (short term); Moody's corporate family rating Baa3 with stable outlook.
- Group standing: "Part of the Bajaj group - one of the oldest & most respected business houses"; regulated by RBI, SEBI and IRDAI.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Group structure] Bajaj Finserv Ltd holds 51.30% of Bajaj Finance (54.67% including promoter & promoter group); BFL in turn holds 86.70% of listed Bajaj Housing Finance Ltd, 100% of Bajaj Financial Securities Ltd and 19.9% of Bajaj Finserv Direct Ltd.
- [New entity] The group structure page lists Bajaj Alternate Investment Management Ltd, which "received its registration certificate from SEBI to act as a Portfolio Manager on April 1, 2026, and received approval to establish funds under Category II of Alternative Investment Funds (AIF) in May 2026" and "will act as the Investment Manager".
- [Disclosure practice] "From Q1 onwards, we are also publishing the investor presentation in markdown (.md) format, making it easier to access and consume by LLMs and digital platforms", framed as a transparency and stakeholder-engagement step.
- [Regulatory] BHFL's PBC stood at 61.46% in Q1 FY27 against a regulatory requirement of 60%; BHFL FY26 carried an exceptional charge of ₹ 13 crore for New Labour Codes.
- [Presentation change] The 19-year snapshot is disclosed twice, "before presentation changes" and "after presentation changes" (NPL recovery netted off from loan losses), producing two different sets of loan-loss, NTI and opex-to-NTI ratios for the same historical years.

business.body: Bajaj Finance Limited is a deposit-taking NBFC-ICC (upper layer) engaged in lending, partnerships and services, payments, and deposit acceptance. The company operates through an omnichannel model spanning 4,098 locations and 242,000 active distribution points, supported by its digital app and web platforms.

latest_quarter.body: NIMs were flat in Q1 and guidance stays at **10–15 bps of moderation** for FY27 — management would not upgrade it despite an analyst pointing out that yields improved (consumer-durable-led mix plus excess liquidity carry) and borrowing costs look range-bound. On funding: BFL's liability maturity is deliberately longer than its asset maturity on a behaviouralised basis, so the *stock* cost of funds fell only ~5bps sequentially while **incremental** market rates have risen 30–60bps. The house view is stabilisation since September with a **slight upward bias**, and both named risks — an unresolved West Asia crisis and a disappointing monsoon — are inflationary. Opex/NTI at 33.4% carries three identifiable loads: the new labour code (10bps / INR60 cr), gold-loan branch build and MFI branch build; strip those and the underlying line is improving, which is why a 25–40bps full-year improvement can be guided while the printed number went up. The three-year framing is the important one: at 200 mn customers, **"NIM could look lower, opex would look lower, credit cost could look lower"** — a deliberate re-shaping of the P&L mix, not a margin warning.

latest_quarter.body:

Loan loss to avg AUF 1.54% (1.31% ex a new INR296 cr macro overlay) vs 1.87% YoY; new Stage 2+3 flow 1.87% vs 1.94%; GNPA 0.96% / NNPA 0.39%, PCR 60%. Gold +112% (4% of AUM, ~1,700 branches), rural/urban consumer +49%/+38% (half SKU price inflation), MSME +2% (pruned). Deposits INR68,500 cr = 15% of balance sheet; CAR 21%, leverage 4.9x. BHFL AUM +24%, PAT +23%, ROE 12.5%; BFSL PAT +22%. FY27 guidance held, not raised: opex/NTI −25–40bps, NIM −10–15bps, gold INR29–31k cr / 2,700–2,800 branches, MSME growth from Q3, 18–20 mn customer adds, digital platform INR50,000 cr, no capital raise. Formal guidance revision promised at the Q2 call.

outlook.body:
- **AUM growth:** the standing **22–24% FY27 corridor** and **23–25% longer-term** frame were put to management twice as candidates for an upgrade. Both times refused: *"it does seem we are much better than the guidance that we gave in March… wait for one more quarter, and we sustain it, then we know. We are in a way to revise."* **A formal guidance revision is explicitly promised at the Q2 FY27 call.**
- **Customer franchise adds:** revised up to **18–20 million** for the year (from 15–17 mn) — cited by the analyst, not contested.
- **NIM:** **moderation of 10–15 bps** for FY27 reaffirmed (Rajeev deferring to the absent CFO's prior guidance). He went out of his way to say the refusal to upgrade is "not lack of confidence."
- **Opex to NTI:** **25–40 bps improvement for FY27** — the single hardest number given on the call.
- **Credit cost:** no numeric FY27 range given; "we, in general, remain quite optimistic about the credit cost outlook for FY '27" and continued improvement expected in the new Stage 2+3 flow metric. Provision coverage held at **60%**.
- **Gold loans:** **2,700–2,800 branches by year-end** (stretch 3,000) and **INR29,000–31,000 cr AUM, all organic**. Mature capacity at 2,800 branches ≈ INR14 cr/branch ≈ **INR37,000–38,000 cr**.
- **MSME:** back into growth momentum **by Q3 FY27**.
- **Balance sheet size:** **INR6,30,000–6,50,000 cr** — used as the denominator justifying the overlay build.
- **Capital:** *"we don't foresee raising capital."* Sequence is explicit — **BHFL dilution first (86.7% → 75%), capital raise only after**, and only if growth accelerates. Profit growth to run **faster than balance-sheet growth**.
- **Digital/AI volumes:** digital platform to deliver **INR50,000 cr of business in FY27**, targeting **INR1,00,000 cr in FY28**. AI voice/text-bot disbursements **INR11,000–12,000 cr in FY27** (INR2,500 cr done in Q1).
- **Dated AI milestones:** custom AI model live for **B2B in Q2 FY27** (unlocking ~0.5 mn customers previously un-acquirable); the **B2C** model by **October–November 2026**; an all-new **consumer AI platform by May–June 2027**; marketing/GEO-SEO acceleration "from November, December".
- **Distribution:** ~**160 branches** to be opened this year (non-gold/MFI), then **170–250 branches every year**, i.e. **4–5% distribution expansion p.a.**
- **New businesses:** **two new lines of business to launch by January–February 2027**.
- **Cost of funds:** *"range bound at these levels only and maybe with a slight upward bias"* (Anand Bagri).
- **Succession:** Rajeev Jain's term runs to March 2028; the decision will be made **December 2027 – January 2028** ("gives us good 18 months").
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
There is no order book; the forward-visibility proxies are branch capacity, customer adds and the digital funnel — all three inflected this quarter.
- **Record INR37,000 cr AUM addition** with growth described as "secular and broad-based" — not carried by one line.
- **Gold loan is the clearest visible pipeline:** 1,700 branches today → 110 adds a month → 2,700–2,800 by March, against a *stated* mature capacity of INR14 cr per branch. That is INR37,000–38,000 cr of latent AUM against INR29,000–31,000 cr guided for this year — the branch estate is being built ahead of the book.
- **MSME is a coiled spring**: pruned deliberately since July last year, +2% now, guided back to growth from Q3 — a mechanical growth add-back in H2 that is not in the current run-rate.
- **Distribution re-opening after a two-year pause.** Non-gold/MFI branch count has been "flat or going down" for 7–8 quarters. Management redid the "bottoms-up" work and concluded India is *not* covered: 160 branches this year, 170–250 p.a. thereafter, with "material outcomes on a 2- to 3-year forward basis."
- **Digital funnel:** INR50,000 cr of business through the digital platform this year, targeted to double to INR1,00,000 cr next year — framed as the shift "from a push business… towards being a **pull** business."

outlook.body:
- **FinAI — the doubling-down.** AI unit expanding **230 → 400 people**, plus **300 more** in the digital platform unit. Q1 delivery: 27 bots live; **45 million customer interactions** analysed via voice/text AI, producing **4 lakh incremental offers and INR517 cr of disbursements** purely from better consumer insight; **20%+ efficiency** in underwriting; AI voice/text bots disbursed **INR2,500 cr** (INR11,000–12,000 cr guided for the year); AI bots now handle **71% of DIY customer-service volumes**; **17 agentic applications deployed out of 118** identified.
- **Custom AI models as a customer-acquisition unlock.** The custom model going live in Q2 is expected to let the B2B business originate **0.5 million customers it could not underwrite before** — a genuinely new addressable pool, not an efficiency claim. B2C version by October–November.
- **Channel mix already material:** of a INR4,000–6,000 cr monthly urban+rural PL book, **17–18% comes from the voice bot** and ~20% from voice-bot-plus-data; gold loan **25%** digital; business loans ~20%.
- **A new consumer AI platform by May–June 2027**, alongside "AI embeddings" being layered into the existing app and web assets business by business.
- **Two new lines of business to launch January–February 2027** (unnamed).
- **Customer-centricity as a formal function** — a dedicated unit, **10 design-thinking units**, primary and secondary research being run in-house ("it doesn't come normally to bankers to do research").

outlook.body:
- Transform into a FinAI (financial AI) enterprise by embedding intelligence across all processes through four dimensions: Enterprise AI, Consumer AI, Agentic AI, and Data AI.
- Maintain a 'Risk-First Approach' by constantly enhancing risk identification and mitigation processes to ensure low GNPA/NNPA and balance-sheet resilience.
- Uphold customer fairness as an inviolable principle, leveraging digital and AI capabilities for transparent and interactive customer journeys.
- Expand geographical presence and digital platform reach to drive customer acquisition and cross-sell across a diversified 27-product suite.
- The dividend policy aims to enhance long-term shareholder value and sustainable growth. The Board endeavours to maintain a stable and steady dividend, targeting a payout range of 15% to 25% of standalone profit after tax, subject to profits, legal provisions, and internal/external factors such as funding needs for expansion, diversification, acquisitions, strategic plans, investments in subsidiaries, and contingency requirements.
- Enhancing customer relationship management to expand customer base, improve retention, and build brand loyalty.
- Upholding business ethics and transparency to build trust, credibility, and support long-term sustainable growth.
- Robust corporate governance practices to strengthen reputation and stakeholder trust.
- Sustainable economic performance to build stakeholder confidence, enhance competitive edge, and promote long-term growth.
- Data privacy and security framework to protect customer information and mitigate cyber threats.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Bajaj Finance continued to expand its physical distribution and product reach across multiple lending verticals during FY2026. In Gold Loans, 350 standalone branches were added, taking the standalone network to 1,314 branches and the overall gold loan branch network to 1,507 branches. The Microfinance group lending business scaled from a pilot to 11 states, covering 41,266 villages through 447 branches. Tractor Financing expanded to nearly 400 locations in five states, up from 200 locations in four states, with relationships built with eight OEMs and a dealer network of over 3,200. Commercial Vehicle Financing now operates in 13 core markets with 165 dealers. Used Car Financing is operational across 57 locations covering over 1,000 channels and dealer outlets. Rural Lending operates across 2,571 rural locations in 22 states and 2 union territories, though the physical footprint was rationalised for efficiency. The strategic partnership with Bharti Airtel scaled meaningfully, with a suite of Bajaj Finance products live on the Airtel Thanks App, disbursing approximately ₹700 crore of loans and issuing around 700,000 Insta EMI Cards during the year.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's resilient domestic demand, with private final consumption expenditure at ~55.7% of GDP, supports lending growth.
- Benign inflation and calibrated monetary easing (repo rate reduced from 6.50% to 5.25%) create a supportive credit environment.
- NBFC credit as a percentage of GDP has risen from 8.9% in FY2015 to 14.6% in FY2025, indicating expanding addressable market.
- Regulatory rationalisation (consolidation into 238 Master Directions) enhances operating environment for well-governed NBFCs.
- Geopolitical tensions and potential commodity price shocks (crude oil, energy costs) pose downside risks to consumer sentiment and housing spends.
